channel.title: Newspin: latest timeline updates
channel.description: Newspin turns the biggest ongoing news stories in India, the US and around the world into clear, sourced timelines: what happened, when, and what comes next.

item.title: SpiceJet: DGCA issues a show-cause notice; shares hit the lower limit
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · India's aviation regulator, the DGCA, has asked SpiceJet to explain why action should not be taken against it, PTI reports, citing a notice dated 17 November. A show-cause notice is a formal warning that gives a company a chance to respond before any penalty. According to the reports, the notice says SpiceJet 'has failed to submit a credible plan for return to service of the grounded aircraft' and that most of its fleet is grounded. It also cites cancellations, poor on-time performance, not flying its approved schedule, uncertainty over renewing mandatory insurance, and concerns raised by overseas regulators about unpaid service providers. SpiceJet has seven days to reply. Its shares fell 5%, the most allowed in a day, to ₹9.74 on the BSE, per Upstox. SpiceJet had not commented, and the BSE asked it for clarification.

item.title: Delhi air: Friday morning: AQI eases to 269 on the season's coldest morning
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · Delhi's average AQI was 269 at 8 am on Friday, per CPCB real-time data reported by Business Standard, down from 289 on Thursday morning. That is 'poor' (201–300). Fourteen of 57 stations were 'very poor' (above 300), led by Sirifort at 348 and JNU at 336; none was 'severe'. Gurugram, at 291, was the most polluted nearby city. The minimum temperature at Safdarjung was 10.5°C, the coldest morning of the season so far, per IMD figures reported by The Week. Stage I and II curbs remain in force.

item.title: RBI rates: Reuters poll: most economists expect a December hike to 5.75%
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · In a Reuters poll taken from 13 to 20 November, 56 of 61 economists expect the RBI to raise the repo rate by 0.25 percentage points to 5.75% at its 2–4 December meeting. Three expect no change and two expect a bigger rise. Most (34 of 46) expect one more rise, to 6%, in February. Economists cite higher energy costs from the Middle East war and a patchy monsoon, and expect inflation to stay above the RBI's 4% target this year and next. This is a forecast by economists, not an RBI decision.

item.title: Rupee: Rupee crosses 93 and closes at a seven-month high of 92.67
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · The rupee closed at 92.67 per dollar on Friday (provisional), 65 paise stronger than Thursday and its strongest level in seven months, PTI reports. During the day it crossed 93 for the first time since 20 April, per Business Today. Dealers credit foreign investors buying Indian shares, lower oil prices (Brent fell 1.82% to $90.31 during the day, per PTI) and a rally in Indian stocks. Business Today says foreign investors have put about $12 billion into Indian shares this month, and also points to exporters selling dollars and possible RBI action. On the two days before, PTI reported closes of 93.44 (provisional) on Wednesday and 93.32 on Thursday.

item.title: India markets: Banks pull Nifty back from a weak open to close above 25,800
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · The Nifty opened about 146 points lower at 25,368, according to Upstox and Liquide, after a sell-off in AI-linked technology shares overnight in the US and Asia. It then recovered to close up 286.30 points (1.12%) at 25,800.60, according to Business Today, Kotak Neo, HDFC Sky and Liquide. The Sensex rose 897.96 points (1.08%) to 83,919.71. HDFC Sky calls it a nine-month high. Reporters credit buying by foreign investors, gains in bank and IT stocks, lower oil prices and a stronger rupee. HDFC Sky says global funds are moving money out of AI-linked stocks and into India. Nifty Bank rose 2.49% to a record close of 64,635.20, per Liquide and Marketcalls, and Nifty IT rose 1.30%, per Kotak Neo. More shares fell than rose on the BSE (1,582 up, 2,456 down), per HDFC Sky. Apollo Hospitals (+5.29%) and Axis Bank (+4.72%) gained the most in the Nifty; Titan (−1.70%) and Tata Steel (−1.60%) fell the most, per HDFC Sky.

item.title: SpiceJet: About three in four SpiceJet flights at the top three airports don't operate
item.description: 19 Nov 2026 · Of 42 SpiceJet flights scheduled on Thursday at Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, 31 were cancelled or did not operate, about 74%, according to Business Standard's analysis of airport data. Delhi airport posted that 'due to operational challenges being faced by SpiceJet airline, some flights may be impacted'. Business Standard says SpiceJet carried about 73,000 domestic passengers in September, down from about 592,000 in January. SpiceJet and the DGCA did not respond to the paper.

item.title: AI this week: Anthropic's shares close 17% above IPO price on first day
item.description: 19 Nov 2026 (US time) · Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq as ANT. The first trade was at $111.50, and the shares closed at $97.17, up 17.1% on the $83 IPO price, per StockTitan and the Motley Fool. It raised about $81.3 billion, per StockTitan. Wider AI stocks fell the same day: Nvidia lost 3.3% and AMD 7.7%, and the S&P 500 fell about 2%.

item.title: Anthropic: Anthropic starts trading on Nasdaq; shares close 17% above the IPO price
item.description: 19 Nov 2026 (US time) · Anthropic's shares began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The IPO was priced at $83 a share, above the $70–78 range. The first trade was at $111.50, about 34% above that price, per StockTitan and StockAnalysis. The shares then fell back and closed at $97.17, up 17.1% on the IPO price, per StockTitan and the Motley Fool. Anthropic sold 980 million Class A shares and raised about $81.3 billion, per StockTitan. The Motley Fool called it the largest IPO in history. The debut came on a day when the S&P 500 fell about 2%.

item.title: US markets: S&P 500 falls 2% for a sixth straight loss; Dow drops about 1,100 points
item.description: 19 Nov 2026 · All three indexes opened higher and held gains through the morning, then turned lower, per 24/7 Wall St. The S&P 500 fell about 2% to about 7,177, its sixth loss in a row and its longest losing run since April 2024, per the Motley Fool. The Dow fell 2.19% and the Nasdaq 2.23%. Reporters linked the fall to talk of further Fed rate rises and worries about high share prices and inflation. Nvidia fell 3.3%. AMD fell 7.7% after a report alleged links to a blacklisted Chinese server maker, per the Motley Fool. Anthropic's shares started trading on the same day and closed 17.1% above their $83 IPO price. Exact opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure.

item.title: US ground stop: FAA pauses router installs; cause still unknown and oversight disputed
item.description: 18–19 Nov (US time) · The FAA has suspended installation of the router model linked to the failure, Engadget reports, and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said the agency still does not know what triggered it. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the same upgrade had 'worked well' 68 times before, blamed the contractor L3Harris for being slow to isolate the problem, and asked the FBI to help examine the router in Arkansas, per AP and Engadget. Bedford said: 'I take full responsibility for it.' The router's maker, HPE, says the routers were 'working exactly as designed', per ABC News. Investigators are checking whether the router was set up wrongly or was faulty, AP reports. Bedford said the contractor's engineer was monitored by an FAA technician; the air traffic technicians' union PASS and two sources dispute that, per Scripps News, and an FAA spokeswoman later said the escort 'is not there while the technician is doing work'. L3Harris declined further comment.

item.title: Air India 171: Government asks the Supreme Court for two to three more weeks
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · The Solicitor General told the Supreme Court that the investigation is at the 'fag end' and asked for two to three more weeks, according to Newsgram, AeroCorner and the Free Press Journal. 'There is no reason why we should delay deliberately,' he said. The petitioners, including the Safety Matters Foundation, objected to repeated delays and want an independent inquiry monitored by the court. The government had earlier said the draft final report would be filed in a sealed cover in October; none of the reports say it has been filed.

item.title: AI this week: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · Google's new mid-priced model costs $3 per million input tokens in its API, less than OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra at $8, per PYMNTS. Google says it ranks third on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index; that is Google's own figure. It is in the Gemini app for paying AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

item.title: AI this week: Reuters: Meta's Muse agent read Signal messages in tests
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · Reuters reports that Meta's Muse agent read Signal messages through phone permissions on Android and Mac, and showed some employees what looked like other users' data. Meta called them 'isolated incidents'.

item.title: AI model tracker: Google: Gemini 4 Neon
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · A mid-priced Gemini 4 model between Carbon and Hydrogen, in the Gemini app for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and in the paid API at $3/$15 per million input/output tokens. Google says it is close to Carbon's quality at lower cost; these are Google's own tests.

item.title: Google Gemini: Gemini 4 Neon, a mid-priced model between Carbon and Hydrogen
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 (US time) · Google releases Gemini 4 Neon. It sits between Gemini 4 Carbon, which Google keeps for the hardest long tasks, and the faster Gemini 4 Hydrogen, per Digital Trends. It replaces Argon in the Gemini app's model picker for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, and is rolling out in the paid Gemini API at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a one-million-token context window. Google says Neon scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, third overall, and costs 32% less per task than Carbon at similar quality; these are Google's own figures.

item.title: Meta AI: Reuters reports privacy slips by the Muse agent
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · Reuters reports that, according to internal posts, Meta's Muse personal agent read users' Signal messages through phone notification permissions on Android and screen tools on Mac. Reuters, Signal and the AI Now Institute repeated this in tests; it was blocked on iPhone. Signal's encryption itself was not broken. Employees also reported Muse showing bank balances and chats that seemed to belong to other users; Reuters could not determine whether they were real or made up. Signal's president called it 'technologically reckless'. A Meta spokesperson called them 'isolated incidents' and said many mix-ups were hallucinations that have been fixed. Meta says Muse has had more than 10 million downloads since September.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Tankers hit near Hormuz; Iran strikes at a Kuwait base; Riyadh tower damaged
item.description: 17–19 Nov 2026 · An ADNOC product tanker was hit by an 'unknown projectile' north of Khasab, Oman, at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one seafarer missing and 11 injured, ADNOC's shipping arm confirmed, per Seatrade Maritime. A second tanker was hit in its engine room near Khasab on 18 November; its crew are safe, per Gulf News and Arab News. Nobody has claimed either attack. On 17 November a US fighter struck what a US official called an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in 'self-defense', after Iranian drones targeted US forces in Bahrain, per TIME. On 18 November Iran attacked Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait, which hosts US forces, and targets in Bahrain; both countries said they repelled the attacks, per The Hill and TIME. Iranian military units separately claimed that tankers hit mines east of Hormuz; this has not been independently confirmed. On 19 November a Houthi attack damaged the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh, with no injuries reported, per Al Jazeera and The National. Despite this, Brent settled at $91.95 on 18 November, down 1.28%, as US stockpiles rose, Reuters reports.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Board sets up a national security and export control committee; Huang to be questioned on 1 December
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia's board created a standing National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to oversee the company's national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risks. It is chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, with directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri, and will meet at least quarterly. Separately, Axios reports Huang will sit for a closed-door, transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China select committees on 1 December, and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter on 2 December. This is not a public hearing.

item.title: OpenAI: Oregon sues over child safety
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · Oregon's attorney general sued OpenAI in state court, seeking more than $2 billion. The state alleges ChatGPT was designed to make users dependent on it, gave 'sycophantic' answers and failed to protect children; these are allegations and no court has ruled. OpenAI said it will 'continue to work with experts to build and strengthen additional safeguards.'

item.title: Budget 2027: Finance Minister begins pre-Budget meetings with industry and experts
item.description: 16–20 Nov 2026 · Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman began pre-Budget consultations for 2027-28, meeting economists first and then groups including small businesses and startups (17 Nov), capital markets and financial firms (18 Nov), IT and infrastructure and energy experts (19 Nov), and labour and employment groups (20 Nov), per UNI and The Tribune. The ministry has not said what was suggested. The Tribune says the Budget is expected on 1 February 2027; the date has not been officially announced.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Justice and Commerce departments confirm a joint probe of Megaspeed
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 (US time) · The US Justice Department and Commerce Department said in a joint statement that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud-computing company at the centre of the Huang reports, and would pursue it to the "fullest extent of the law" for "any criminal conduct that may have occurred", per ABC News. ABC reports Commerce's inquiry began in 2024 and that Nvidia put Megaspeed on its 'no sell' list in June 2025. Megaspeed has not been charged with any crime.

item.title: Russian oil: Russian oil set for a smaller share in November as discounts return
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 · Kpler estimates that India is importing about 1.7 million barrels a day of Russian crude in November, down from about 2.07 million in October, ThePrint reports. Brazilian and Venezuelan supplies are rising. Russian Urals crude has moved from costing more than the global Brent benchmark in early October to selling at a discount in November, per Kpler data cited by ThePrint and Argus figures cited by The Moscow Times.

item.title: Delhi air: Thursday morning: AQI rises to 289, near the 'very poor' line
item.description: 19 Nov 2026 · Delhi's average AQI was 289 at 8:30 am on Thursday, up from 212 earlier, per CPCB data reported by IANS. That is still 'poor' (201–300), but several stations were in the 'very poor' band (301–400), including JNU at 367, Sirifort at 363 and ITO at 356. Wednesday's daily average was 232. On Wednesday the air quality early warning system said weather over the next two days could stop pollution from clearing.

item.title: India markets: Autos and banks lift Nifty above 25,500 after a weak start
item.description: 19 Nov 2026 · The Nifty opened lower and closed up 286.35 points (1.14%) at 25,514.30, according to Business Today and Kotak Neo. The Sensex rose 989.94 points (1.21%) to 83,021.75. Business Today says it was the Nifty's first close above 25,500 since 26 February. Marketcalls says the market started lower after minutes from the US Federal Reserve pointed to more US rate rises, then autos, banks and consumer goods stocks pulled it up. Business Today and Kotak Neo say falling copper and other metal prices should lower costs for carmakers and appliance makers. The Nifty Auto index rose 4.40% and Nifty IT fell 1.10%, per Kotak Neo and Marketcalls. Maruti Suzuki gained 7.30%, the best in the Nifty; Infosys (−1.52%) fell the most, per Marketcalls.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Shares fall about 3% the day after results
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 (US close) · Nvidia shares closed down 2.89% on Wednesday, per StockTitan, giving up their after-hours gain from the night before. Yahoo Finance reports it was the fifth day of losses in a row, and that the strong results did not outweigh worries about Huang's departure.

item.title: AI this week: Anthropic's IPO reportedly priced at $83, above the range
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 (US time) · Anthropic priced its shares at $83, above the $70–78 range, according to Reuters, Bloomberg and CNBC, citing people familiar with the matter. That values it at about $1.5 trillion including all shares and options, per TechCrunch. Trading on Nasdaq as ANT is due to start on 19 November. Anthropic had not announced the price itself.

item.title: Anthropic: IPO reportedly priced at $83 a share, above the range
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 (US time) · Anthropic priced its shares at $83 each, above its $70–78 range, according to Reuters, Bloomberg and CNBC, citing people familiar with the matter. At that price the company is valued at about $1.5 trillion including all shares and options, per TechCrunch and the Motley Fool. A source told Reuters the company also sold more shares than the 825 million first planned, but the new number and the final amount raised have not been disclosed. The shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Thursday 19 November. Anthropic had not announced the price itself at the time of these reports.

item.title: US markets: S&P 500 slips for a fifth day; Dow falls 1.1%, Nasdaq rises
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · The S&P 500 fell 0.23% to 7,323.63, its fifth loss in a row, per Yahoo Finance and StockTitan. The Dow fell 561 points while the Nasdaq rose 0.42%. Health insurers fell after a US government proposal to step up anti-fraud checks on Medicare Advantage plans. Minutes of the Fed's last meeting showed nearly all officials expect further rate rises may be needed, per the Motley Fool. Nvidia fell 2.9% the day after its results. Amazon, an Anthropic investor, rose before Anthropic's share sale. The opening level could not be confirmed from two reports, so this day has no gap figure.

item.title: SpiceJet: Board approves raising up to ₹5,500 crore
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · SpiceJet's board approved raising up to ₹5,500 crore, in one or more rounds, through new shares, debt with warrants or other securities, the airline said in an exchange filing reported by Business Today, Angel One and Upstox. Routes could include a share sale to institutions (QIP), a rights issue or a preferential allotment. The board also approved raising the company's authorised share capital, the maximum it can issue, from ₹2,000 crore to ₹7,500 crore. Both need shareholder and regulatory approval. Chairman Ajay Singh said the fundraise is 'an important opportunity to rebuild the airline'. The board was told about talks with possible new investors and asked management to close them quickly; no investors were named. The shares rose 5% to ₹9.97, the daily limit.

item.title: Delhi air: Wednesday morning: AQI 214, still 'poor'
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · Delhi's average AQI was 214 at 7 am, down from 246 at the same time on Tuesday, per CPCB real-time data reported by Business Standard. None of 58 stations was 'severe'; one was above 300. That is still in the 'poor' band (201–300), which can cause breathing discomfort on long exposure. An earlier IITM forecast said air could turn 'very poor' on Wednesday; that had not happened by the morning.

item.title: India markets: Profit booking ends a two-day rise; metals and Titan drag
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · The Nifty opened 64.25 points lower and closed down 159.45 points (0.63%) at 25,227.95, according to DSIJ and Angel One. The Sensex fell 500.38 points (0.61%) to 82,031.81. HDFC Sky and Kotak Neo say investors booked profits after a strong November rally. HDFC Sky says a stronger US dollar and expectations of more US rate rises hurt metal prices. Thirteen of 16 sector indices fell, HDFC Sky reports: consumer durables lost about 3% and metals about 2.5%. Titan fell 5.3%, the worst in the Nifty; SBI (+2.4%) and Cipla (+2%) were the top gainers.

item.title: SpiceJet: No SpiceJet departures from Mumbai for more than 12 hours
item.description: 17–18 Nov · No SpiceJet flight left Mumbai airport from 7 pm on Tuesday, and the halt was still going on more than 12 hours later, according to Aviation Jeta, Amar Ujala and Dynamite News. Hundreds of passengers, on domestic and international routes, were stuck overnight, and some protested at the airline's counter. Aviation Jeta, citing airport sources, says 12 scheduled departures from Mumbai had been cancelled by Tuesday. SpiceJet had not issued a statement or given a reason by Wednesday morning. Passengers say they were not told about the delays or new departure times.

item.title: Delhi air: Stage III curbs lifted; Stage I and II stay
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), which runs Delhi-NCR's pollution action plan (GRAP), revoked Stage III curbs with immediate effect, citing a falling trend in daily AQI. The daily average reached 204 on Tuesday, per CAQM's sub-committee. Stage I and II measures continue across the NCR. Delhi-registered BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel cars can drive again, Business Today reports. Delhi's education department told schools to hold classes in person for all students, per Business Standard. CAQM cited forecasts that air will stay 'poor' or 'very poor' in the coming days.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Huang says he would be 'honored' to return as CEO if the board wants him
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 (US time) · In his first public statement since resigning, posted on X and sent to news outlets, Huang said he had "made serious mistakes" in his personal life and was committed to cooperating with the board's independent investigation. He said employees, investors, partners and customers had called for him to come back, and that he would be "honored" to return as CEO if the board decides that is in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America. CBS News, citing a person familiar with the board's thinking, reports the board is not interested in reinstating him in any role.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: First results without Huang: revenue doubles; board chair says Huang won't return
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion for August–October, up 103% from a year earlier, in its first results under interim CEO Colette Kress. Data centre sales, mostly AI chips, were $107.6 billion. Profit was $65.3 billion. Nvidia expects about $130 billion in sales next quarter, assuming no data centre chip sales to China. "Our momentum is real," Kress said. On the earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones said "the Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO", per Constellation Research; CBS News, citing a person familiar with the board's thinking, also reports the board is against his return. Shares fell 0.44% in regular trading, then rose nearly 3% after hours, per CBS News.

item.title: AI this week: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra, for the hardest professional work such as documents, slides and coding, and GPT-6.2 Sol, a cheaper everyday model. Both are in ChatGPT and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users, and in the API. Astra costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens; Sol $2 and $10. OpenAI's own charts show gains over earlier versions on most tests. Independent results are mixed, per VentureBeat: Artificial Analysis ranks Astra second overall behind Claude Fable 5.2, and some well-known developers criticised the release.

item.title: AI this week: Nvidia's sales double; board says Huang won't return
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103% on a year earlier, and expects about $130 billion next quarter. It was the first report under interim CEO Colette Kress. Board chair Harvey Jones said on the call that the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang, per Constellation Research. Shares rose after hours.

item.title: AI this week: Microsoft launches its own coding and security models
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · At its Ignite conference, Microsoft released a new set of in-house MAI models, including MAI Code 2 for programming, a cybersecurity model offered at first to a limited group of customers, and image and speech models. Microsoft says MAI Code 2 reaches 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's quality at about 40% of the price, and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's at 5% of the price, on its chosen coding tests; Reuters describes it as almost matching rivals at a fraction of the cost. MAI Code 2 is available in GitHub Copilot, per TestingCatalog. Microsoft also announced an AI Transparency Initiative with more than 40 organisations to develop open standards for checking AI models.

item.title: AI model tracker: OpenAI: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · OpenAI's new top model, Astra, and a cheaper everyday model, Sol, in ChatGPT, Codex and the API. Astra costs $8/$40 per million input/output tokens. OpenAI reports gains on most of its tests; independent results are mixed, per VentureBeat.
